subject: Redlines: IP scope, training opt-ins, and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Kelsey Martin <kelsey@novum.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Notes on your redlines: IP scope & training language

Kelsey —

Thanks for sending the redlines. I skimmed the MSA/order form and highlighted three areas we should align on before we route to procurement/legal: (1) output ownership and whether "productization" of customer outputs is allowed, (2) training/data use (opt-in vs. telemetry-only permit), and (3) evidence you need from us to satisfy your security/compliance checks.

High-level responses:
- Redwood can accept a narrow customer "productization" carveout for outputs derived from the customer's inputs, provided we retain a non-exclusive, anonymized telemetry license to improve the service (not to create derivative models that compete with a customer).
- For training: we propose a telemetry-only license by default and an explicit opt-in checkbox on the order form to allow model retraining with customer data. That makes the operational flow cleaner and preserves customer choice.
- Evidence handoff: we can provide SOC 2 attestation, redacted telemetry samples, and a short technical attestation describing retention and purge policies. I can assemble a two-week delivery plan.

Can you confirm which of the redline clauses are must-haves vs. nice-to-haves for Novum? If you can mark those, we’ll prioritize the proposed language.

Attached: Novum-redlines_MSA_v1.docx (received).

Thanks — talk soon,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Hannah —

Appreciate the quick read-through. Two clarifications from our side:
1) Productization carveout: Novum will not agree to any language that allows Redwood (or third parties) to create or offer a model trained on our customer data that is then sold to others. We can consider a narrow exception that allows "feature extraction" for internal analytics inside our product, but not model retraining for general-purpose models.
2) Telemetry/opt-in: we prefer an opt-in model for any training (explicit consent on the order form). Telemetry-only processing is acceptable only if it is strictly aggregated and irreversible; we need wording to that effect.

Aram (cc) is our GC and will review any proposed counter-language for legal risk. From procurement’s perspective, an evidence bundle (SOC 2 + retention policy + dataflow diagram) should be provided before we sign.

Thanks,
Kelsey Martin

Subject: Re: Fwd: Notes on your redlines: IP scope & training language — proposed language

Hannah / team —

Thanks for sending this over. Draft guidance below — I’ll circulate a redline later today:

1) Productization carveout: Proposed compromise text — "Customer may use Outputs to develop and deploy Customer-facing features for Customer's products and services; Redwood shall not use Customer-specific Training Data to create or offer standalone models to third parties that are substantially derived from Customer Training Data." This tracks Novum’s ask while allowing us to retain typical improvements path.

2) Training/telemetry: We should classify two buckets: (i) "Telemetry": aggregated usage metrics and anonymized model telemetry used for service quality improvements (non-reversible, non-identifying); (ii) "Training Data": customer-provided datasets or explicit opt-in that may be used to improve models. Default should be telemetry-only; training requires affirmative order-form opt-in.

3) Evidence handoff: We will provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), a short retention/purge attestation, and a sample of anonymized telemetry (redacted). Delivery SLA: 10 business days after countersignature. If procurement requires additional artifacts, they should list them in the attached checklist.

I will attach: Redwood-Proposed-IP-language_v2.docx with tracked changes and a short redline summary.

—Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
